bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM launches water metro service on Ganga river in Patna - ET Infra
bihar_raw_news.content: Urban Transportation 1 min Read Bihar CM launches water metro service on Ganga river in Patna "The service is also expected to provide commuters with an alternate route to the congested Ashok Rajpath," an official said. PTI Published On Nov 10, 2026 at 08:48 PM IST Set ETInfra as your preferred source on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment The fare is ₹50 for each adult. Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday launched a catamaran service on the Ganga river between Digha Ghat and Gandhi Ghat in Patna , aiming to promote eco-friendly tourism and provide an alternative mode of transport. Flagging off the water metro service from Digha Ghat, the chief minister said the state tourism department's initiative would offer tourists and locals a modern and convenient transport facility while boosting river tourism . "The service is also expected to provide commuters with an alternate route to the congested Ashok Rajpath," an official said. The 50-seater vessel is equipped with a hybrid engine , primarily operating on electric power, helping minimise air, water and noise pollution, said a statement issued by the Chief Minister's Office. It has facilities such as air-conditioning, a public announcement system, toilets and wheelchair accessibility. The service will operate between Digha and Gandhi Ghat, with plans to extend it to Kangan Ghat in the future. Fast and shore charging facilities have been installed at Digha and Gandhi Ghats. The fare is ₹50 for each adult. Children below five years can travel free, while those aged between five and 12 will be charged half the adult fare, the statement said. Tickets are currently available at the counter at Digha Ghat, with online booking expected to be introduced soon. Comments What are your thoughts?

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Building Bylaws 2026 Bring 30-Day Deemed Approval - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Building Bylaws 2026 Bring 30-Day Deemed Approval Breaking News Bihar Building Bylaws 2026 Bring 30-Day Deemed Approval By Ananya Sharma November 11, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp The Bihar cabinet has approved the Building Bylaws 2026, introducing deemed approval of building maps if local urban bodies do not clear applications within 30 days and replacing the rules framed in 2014. The new regulations were approved on Tuesday following a proposal from the urban development and housing department, Cabinet secretariat additional chief secretary Arwind Kumar Choudhary said, according to a report by the Times of India. The rules classify residential and commercial buildings according to risk, introduce restrictions through a negative list for builders and set out provisions linked to floor area ratio (FAR). Buildings up to 10 metres in height have been classified as low risk, those between 10 metres and 24 metres as medium risk, and structures above 24 metres as high risk. The classification is intended to establish different regulatory requirements based on the scale and potential risks associated with a building. The bylaws allow an approach road of up to 3.7 metres and require a setback on only one side in specified circumstances, enabling emergency vehicles to access a building from the rear. Parking space will be calculated at 15 square metres per vehicle. The rules also allow building map approvals to be revalidated for five years, with automatic revalidation on payment of the prescribed fee. Owners of existing buildings will be able to obtain permits by paying the prescribed fee and submitting building maps. The cabinet decision also incorporates fire safety provisions into the building permit process, making fire-related compliance part of the approval framework. The regulations offer additional development potential for buildings that secure green-building certification. Buildings with three-star certification will be eligible for an additional 5% FAR, while four-star and five-star buildings will receive 10% and 15% additional FAR, respectively. FAR determines the total floor area that can be constructed on a plot relative to its size. The deemed approval provision could reduce delays for applicants where local urban bodies do not decide applications within the 30-day period. Its operation will depend on how applications are received, scrutinised and recorded, and on the procedures that urban bodies adopt for enforcing the new rules. The cabinet announcement, as reported, did not specify how disputes or incomplete applications will be handled under the deemed-clearance mechanism. The cabinet also approved decisions outside the building regulations. Dearness allowance for government employees, pensioners and family pensioners covered by the fifth, sixth and seventh pay commissions was increased retrospectively from July 1. The revisions raise the rates from 483% to 497% for the fifth pay commission, from 262% to 269% for the sixth and from 60% to 63% for the seventh. The changes will impose an additional annual burden of Rs 1,088 crore on the state exchequer. In another decision, the cabinet approved the Bihar Artificial Intelligence Mission. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar IAS Promotions Lift Key Urban Officials to Higher Ranks
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar IAS Promotions Lift Key Urban Officials to Higher Ranks Breaking News Bihar IAS Promotions Lift Key Urban Officials to Higher Ranks By Ananya Sharma November 11, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp The Bihar government promoted 30 IAS officers on Tuesday, elevating two senior officials to additional chief secretary rank and placing officers associated with road construction, disaster management, district administration and the Patna Municipal Corporation in higher grades. Santosh Kumar Mall, principal secretary in the disaster management department, and Pankaj Kumar, principal secretary in the home department, were promoted to the rank of additional chief secretary, according to the report. The elevation comes as Bihar’s administrative structure continues to manage responsibilities spanning public safety, civic services and infrastructure delivery. Road construction department secretary Pankaj Kumar Pal was placed in the rank of principal secretary. The department is responsible for a major part of the state’s road infrastructure administration, although the report did not specify any change in his posting or announce any new project linked to the promotion. The government also promoted several officers to secretary rank. They include Himanshu Kumar Sharma, special secretary in the science, technology and technical education department; Shirsat Kapil Ashok, managing director of Comfed; Nilesh Ramchandra Deore; Ujjwal Kumar, special secretary in the rural development department; Naresh Jha, settlement officer in Katihar; Brajesh Kumar, settlement officer in Madhepura; Navin Kumar, special secretary in the prohibition, excise and registration department; and Udyan Mishra, special secretary in the tourism department. The list also includes officers whose work is directly connected with district-level administration and urban service delivery. Nalanda district magistrate Udita Singh, Samastipur district magistrate Roshan Kushwaha and Gaya district magistrate Shashank Shubhankar were elevated to the rank of special secretary. District magistrates oversee coordination between state departments and local administrations, but the report did not indicate whether the officers would retain their current postings. Panchayati raj additional secretary Aditya Prakash and revenue and land reforms additional secretary Amit Kumar Pandey were also promoted to special secretary rank. Their departments deal with local government administration and land-related processes, both of which affect how public infrastructure, development activity and civic expansion are administered across Bihar. Yashpal Meena, commissioner of the Patna Municipal Corporation, was among the officers elevated to special secretary rank. The promotion affects his administrative rank; the supplied report does not state that he has been transferred or that the corporation’s responsibilities have changed. The municipal commissioner’s position is responsible for the functioning of Patna’s civic administration, including the implementation of municipal services within the city. The promotions therefore span state departments, district administrations and a major municipal body. The order, as reported, changes the officers’ ranks but does not provide details on revised postings, additional responsibilities, implementation dates or any departmental reshuffle that may follow. Further administrative orders would be required to establish whether the promotions lead to changes in assignments. national_raw_news.content: The Supreme Court has asked WhatsApp and other intermediaries to apprise it about their proposed measures to prevent digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes in the country. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant asked WhatsApp and similar intermediaries to simultaneously submit their proposals to the I4C (Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre). The order regarding it uploaded on the website with regard to the hearing conducted on 29th of last month in a suo motu case titled ‘Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents’, The bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, has listed the plea for further consideration on 23rd of this month. WhatsApp, had told the bench the platform had taken preventive measures, including action against 9,400 accounts, and would file an affidavit detailing the steps undertaken. The top court, on October 29, had said financial institutions must be held accountable for digital arrest scams and other cyber frauds, emphasising that banks should be required to compensate victims for losses suffered where an investigation establishes that the fraud occurred due to the institution’s failure to exercise due diligence. The bench also directed the law enforcement agencies of all states and Union territories to submit reports detailing FIRs registered in digital arrest scam cases and the investigations arising from them.

national_raw_news.title: President Murmu stresses people-centric policing, urges IPS officers to address public grievances
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has urged IPS officers to prioritise alleviating the fears of socially or economically weaker individuals who generally lack access to senior officials, and addressing their grievances. Addressing, Probationers of the 2025 batch of Indian Police Service today at Rashtrapati Bhava the President said for the citizens, police officers and constables are symbols of governance. She said, people perceive the governance to be good when the police system functions well. The President said that the People feel immensely supported when a police officer listens to their grievances with sensitivity and attentiveness. The President stated that some of the employees in the system may be more proficient in the use of technology than the senior officers. She advised the officer trainees to not hesitate to learn even from the most junior members of their team. She urged them to encourage public participation and teamwork in their working style. She said that by prioritising the welfare of their team members, they will enhance their capabilities and enthusiasm. The President said that the police officers would derive a high level of authority from the laws and rules related to policing. However, they will earn real respect from the people, based on their performance and value system. She said that they should have a sense of commitment to serving citizens rather than a sense of superiority over them. She highlighted the need for police officers to always stay ahead of the criminals who use state-of-the-art technologies.

national_raw_news.title: BCCI announces Smriti Mandhana led squads for upcoming all-format tour of South Africa 09 Nov 2026 | 8:00 PM 284
national_raw_news.content: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) Women’s Selection Committee has announced squads for the upcoming all-format tour of South Africa in December. Smriti Mandhana is set to lead the side across all three formats. India will play one Test, three ODIs and three T20Is during the tour, which will begin with the Test match in Gqeberha on 9th December. The ODI series will start on 16th December in Paarl, followed by the second match in Cape Town on 19th December and the third in Bloemfontein on 22nd December. The three-match T20I series will begin on December 26 in Benoni. The second and third matches are scheduled to be played in Potchefstroom. Deepti Sharma has been named vice-captain of the Test and ODI squads, while Shafali Verma will serve as vice-captain in the T20I format. The Test squad features 15 players, including Harmanpreet Kaur, Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh, Yastika Bhatia, Sneh Rana and Kranti Gaud. The ODI squad also comprises 15 players, with Vaishnavi Sharma included in place of Sneh Rana from the Test squad. The T20I squad has 17 players, with Shafali Verma as vice-captain. Niki Prasad, G. Kamalini, Anushka Sharma, Prema Rawat, Amanjot Kaur, Renuka Singh Thakur and Arundhati Reddy are also part of the squad.

national_raw_news.title: Trump says his immigration policy ‘too tough’ after midterm drubbing
national_raw_news.content: US President Donald Trump acknowledged that his immigration policy was “too tough” after a severe drubbing in the midterm elections and said he was ready to work with the Democratic Party in the years ahead. Democrats won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections, flipping several Republican-held seats in a sweeping setback for Trump. The results reflected voter dissatisfaction with his handling of the immigration issue, the economy, the Iran war and rising living costs. “I think it was too tough. I think it might be too tough,” Trump told CBS’ 60 Minutes in response to a question on his administration’s deportation policy. The interview was recorded on Friday and telecast on Sunday evening. Soon after the interview was recorded, Trump appointed Stephen Miller, known for his strong views against immigration, as his Chief of Staff, raising questions about whether the President would significantly soften his approach. Asked about the reasons for Republicans’ resounding defeat, Trump echoed the conventional wisdom that it was due to the Iran war and gas prices, while also pointing to hostility towards Israel as a factor. “They didn’t like the war,” Trump said. “They didn’t like the fact that gasoline went up because I had it down at a low. And there’s a great dislike, incredibly, for Israel.” The President said his immigration crackdown had “both helped and hurt” him at the polls. Trump said he believed he “got an A+ for closing up the border” and “very high marks for getting the bad ones out”. “But I get hurt because we also took people that had good jobs, that created one violation, or breaking of the law, and that was that they came into the country illegally,” he said. “Now, there is a large part of the country that thinks that they should be put out. And there’s a large part of the country that thinks that they should be allowed to stay if they’re good people working in a landscaping company, or working in a hotel, or doing something, right? And in some cases, paying taxes. “I think it was too tough,” the Republican leader reiterated. Asked what he thought would happen after his death, Trump said, “I hope I’m missed.” He also described himself as a “religious person” and said he hoped to go to heaven. (PTI)

national_raw_news.title: Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 records sales of Rs 55.46 lakh at Dilli Haat, showcases artisans’ craftsmanship
national_raw_news.content: The ongoing Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA, in the national capital, has recorded cumulative sales of approximately ₹55.46 lakh between November 1 and 8, reflecting strong public response and growing market opportunities for artisans from disadvantaged communities. Organised by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, the 15-day fair will continue until November 15. It provides a platform for artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase and market their products to a wider audience. The sales were recorded by four participating corporations: the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) and National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC). The Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022. Over the years, more than 1,000 artisans from SC, OBC and Safai Karamchari communities have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and sell their products. The initiative aims to promote self-employment, encourage entrepreneurship and support the socio-economic empowerment of beneficiary communities. Organised around the theme ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’, the current edition features more than 130 stalls across seven thematic zones: कला आँगन, प्रकाश चौक, पूजा पथ, सजावट बाज़ार, घराना, स्वाद चौक and मंच. The exhibition showcases a wide range of handicrafts, handloom products, traditional textiles, festive decorations, lamps, home décor items and other indigenous creations. To help beneficiaries participate, the Ministry provides free stalls, travel expenses, daily allowances and transportation facilities for their goods. These measures are intended to reduce financial and logistical barriers and enable artisans to reach new customers and markets. The fair also promotes wider market access through initiatives such as Bharat TULIP, which connects artisans with e-commerce platforms, and Purple Fest, which highlights the creativity and capabilities of persons with disabilities while encouraging inclusion and equal opportunities. Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Virendra Kumar, Minister of State Ramdas Athawale, Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya, and Secretary of the Ministry Sudhansh Pant have visited the Mela. They toured the stalls, appreciated the craftsmanship and interacted with participating artisans, reiterating the government’s focus on inclusive entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihood opportunities. Cultural programmes held every evening at the Mela’s Manch are another major attraction. Artists and performers from different states present folk dances, traditional music and regional art forms, offering visitors an opportunity to experience India’s cultural diversity on a common platform. The fair has been drawing families, young visitors and other members of the public, who are exploring traditional products while supporting artisans and their efforts towards entrepreneurship, economic empowerment and self-reliance. (PIB)

IMPCC focuses on media coordination November 10, 2026 DIMAPUR: The 6th Inter-Media Publicity Coordination Committee (IMPCC), Nagaland Chapter, meeting was held on November 9 at the Directorate of Census Operations, Kohima. According to a press release, the meeting was chaired by Ella Kayina, Head of Programme, Akashvani Kohima, in the presence of Dr. Keneilhoutuolie Miachieo, Director of Census Operations, Nagaland. Officials from the Census Department, Information & Public Relations (IPR), MyGov/My Bharat, National Statistics Office (NSO), Akashvani, Regional News Unit (RNU), Akashvani and Doordarshan, PRO Defence, Central Bureau of Communication (CBC) and Press Information Bureau (PIB) attended the meeting. The meeting deliberated on ways to strengthen inter-media coordination and public outreach across the State. Members representing various departments highlighted their key activities and sought cooperation from other departments to enhance the reach and impact of their publicity programmes. It was decided that the various initiatives undertaken by IMPCC member organisations would be brought onto a common platform to ensure better coordination and wider dissemination of information. The committee also resolved to converge programmes of government broadcasting agencies such as Akashvani and Doordarshan, along with PIB outreach initiatives such as Varta and Vartalap, to maximise public engagement and outreach. Further, the meeting decided to organise a one-day outdoor programme in the coming days to strengthen coordination and foster camaraderie among IMPCC members.
